entries.name: HYG Database
entries.catalog: HYG Database v4.1 (astronexus)
entries.description: Positions, apparent magnitudes, and B−V colors for the real nearby-star field in /explore's Stellar Neighborhood. Merges the Hipparcos, Yale Bright Star, and Gliese catalogues.
entries.license_rationale: Published by astronexus under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International.

entries.name: Constellation figures (d3-celestial)
entries.catalog: d3-celestial constellation lines (Olaf Frohn) — modern IAU figures
entries.description: The modern IAU constellation stick-figures, drawn in /explore's stellar neighborhood and in each named star's finder chart. Star positions are our own (from HYG); this provides the line pattern.
entries.license_rationale: Permissive BSD-3-Clause, used with attribution. The underlying constellation figures are traditional public-domain astronomy (IAU).

entries.name: GCAT — General Catalog of Space Objects
entries.catalog: GCAT (Jonathan C. McDowell, planet4589.org)
entries.description: Agency-grade launch log used as the trunk source for the launches calendar — dates, vehicles, and payload records for historical and current spaceflights.
entries.license_rationale: Released by Jonathan C. McDowell under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International; citation is a ship-gate (PRD-020 M14).

entries.name: Launch Library 2 — The Space Devs
entries.catalog: Launch Library 2 API (TheSpaceDevs)
entries.description: Upcoming-launch gap-fill aggregator for the launches calendar, used where agency-direct sources do not yet cover a launch. A leaf source, not the trunk (PRD-020).
entries.license_rationale: LL2 terms: free use, attribution encouraged but not mandatory. Always cited regardless, per Orrery editorial discipline.

entries.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive
entries.catalog: Planetary Systems Composite Parameters (pscomppars)
entries.description: Confirmed exoplanet orbital elements (period, semi-major axis, eccentricity), radii, masses, and discovery metadata for the host stars rendered as BodyScene mini-orreries in /explore’s Stellar Neighborhood.
entries.license_rationale: Operated by Caltech/IPAC under contract with NASA; the Archive data are U.S. Government works in the public domain, free to reuse with acknowledgement.
entries.acknowledgement: This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program.

entries.name: OpenNGC
entries.catalog: NGC/IC catalogue (Messier subset)
entries.description: Positions (RA/Dec J2000), object types, magnitudes, and common names for the Messier catalogue plus the NGC/IC objects rendered as deep-sky billboards and labelled dots in /explore’s Known Universe. A dozen famous non-catalogue objects (Cartwheel, Tycho's SNR, the Horsehead, Cassiopeia A) carry explicit standard J2000 positions.
entries.license_rationale: OpenNGC is released under CC-BY-SA-4.0; free to reuse with attribution and share-alike. We vendor a distilled snapshot and credit the catalogue here and in /colophon.
entries.acknowledgement: OpenNGC (M. Verga), built from NED, HyperLEDA, SIMBAD, HEASARC and H. Corwin’s NGC/IC notes; licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

entries.name: GRAVITY Collaboration · Event Horizon Telescope
entries.catalog: Galactic-centre astrometry
entries.description: Real astrometry underpinning /explore’s Milky Way schematic: the Sun's distance to the Galactic Centre (R₀ ≈ 8.18 kpc, GRAVITY Collaboration 2019) and the mass of Sagittarius A* (≈ 4.3 million solar masses, GRAVITY Collaboration 2022; imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope 2022). The Galaxy's spiral positions are schematic; these facts are cited and real.
entries.license_rationale: Published scientific measurements from the GRAVITY Collaboration (A&A) and the EHT/ESO release, reusable with attribution. Values only — no imagery embedded; the Milky Way view is our own procedural schematic.

entries.name: Event Horizon Telescope · published black-hole parameters
entries.catalog: Black-hole masses, distances & spins
entries.description: Cited parameters for /explore’s geodesic gravitational-lensing renders: M87* (first imaged, EHT 2019), Sagittarius A* (EHT 2022; GRAVITY mass), and Cygnus X-1 (stellar-mass, mass revised upward by Miller-Jones et al. 2021). Gargantua is labelled fiction (Kip Thorne's Interstellar model). The lensing image is our own geodesic ray-trace — no observatory imagery is embedded.
entries.license_rationale: Published measurements (EHT collaboration papers + peer-reviewed literature), reusable with attribution. Parameter values only; the black-hole visual is procedurally ray-traced from the Schwarzschild geodesic equation.

references.l: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration 2019 (paper VI), ApJ 875, L6: 2019ApJ...875L...6E

entries.name: CelesTrak
entries.catalog: NORAD GP element sets (gp.php API)
entries.description: Two-line element sets for the ISS (NORAD 25544) and Tiangong (48274), refreshed daily and cached, that drive the Physics Lab's satellite-pass prediction (when the station next flies over you, how high, from which bearing).
entries.license_rationale: The underlying element sets originate from US Space Command (public domain); CelesTrak redistributes them and requests attribution as the source, which we give here.

entries.name: NASA JPL · IAU reference constants
entries.catalog: JPL Keplerian planetary elements (Standish) + IAU/EGM96/IUGG constants
entries.description: The authoritative constants the Physics Lab kernel computes from: JPL's Keplerian elements for approximate planetary positions (Standish), IAU gravitational parameters and precession series, the EGM96 geopotential constant, and IUGG mean radii. The Lab's numbers are ours; these reference values are cited and real.
entries.license_rationale: JPL/NASA reference data is US-Government public domain; the IAU/IUGG constants are published international-standard reference values, reusable with citation.
